![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The `set_player` method is currently only called on the server. Since the `Player` scenes (`BOTINI_SCENE` and `BOSS_SCENE`) were removed from the global `PlayerSpawner` in `game.tscn`, they will not be automatically instantiated on clients. Furthermore, the `synchronizer.root_path` is set locally on the server and is not replicated to clients. 

This means clients will have a `MultiplayerClient` node but no `Player` child, and their `MultiplayerSynchronizer` will be looking for properties on a non-existent node, breaking multiplayer synchronization. 

To fix this, you should either:
1. Add a `MultiplayerSpawner` to the `MultiplayerClient` scene configured to spawn the player scenes.
2. Use a replicated variable (e.g., `player_type`) with a setter that instantiates the correct player scene on all peers.

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

Removing the `Player` and `Boss` scenes from the `PlayerSpawner` prevents them from being replicated to clients. In the new architecture, these nodes are added as children of `MultiplayerClient`, but since `MultiplayerClient` is not a spawn path for any spawner, the children are never created on remote peers. This is a critical issue that breaks the game's multiplayer functionality.

## Code Review

This pull request adds a multiplayer API reference and refactors the networking system by introducing a MultiplayerClient class to manage player instances and their synchronization, moving away from per-player synchronizers to a centralized approach with manual position interpolation. Significant issues were identified during review, including a break in player replication because character scenes were removed from the global spawner without being added to a new one. Other feedback points to potential server crashes due to missing null checks in the combat manager, name collision risks when despawning players that require using remove_child before queue_free, and the presence of a debug push_warning in the lobby UI.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

When replacing an existing player, calling `queue_free()` is not sufficient to avoid name collisions in the same frame because `queue_free()` is deferred. If a new player node is added immediately after (as happens in `PlayerManager.spawn_round_players`), Godot will detect a name collision and rename the new node (e.g., to `123@2`). This breaks multiplayer synchronization which relies on consistent node paths.

You should explicitly remove the child from the tree before calling `queue_free()`.

```
	if is_instance_valid(player):
		remove_child(player)
		player.queue_free()
		player = null
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `client` variable obtained from `players.get(owner_id)` can be `null` if the peer ID is not found in the dictionary. Accessing `client.player` without a validity check will cause a runtime error and crash the server.

```
	var client: MultiplayerClient = players.get(owner_id)
	if not is_instance_valid(client) or not is_instance_valid(client.player) or not client.player.is_alive:
		return
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

This `push_warning` appears to be a debug statement that should be removed before merging.

```
		_on_host_pressed()
```
